target_customer: Regional airlines and aircraft operators buying hydrogen-electric propulsion systems or converted aircraft
problem: Battery electric aircraft have short range and fossil fuel aircraft emit carbon. Stralis aimed to retrofit and later build hydrogen-electric aircraft with ten times the range of battery electric.
business_model: Aircraft and propulsion system sales and conversions, with letters of intent from airlines; funded by grants and equity

founders.name: Stuart Johnstone
founders.background_notes: YC page says he and Criner met in 2017 at magniX and that he worked on superconducting magnets for MRI early in his career.

exit.reason: Company said the hydrogen-electric aviation market is still forming and it could not wait for it to mature; coverage also cites certification costs, hydrogen supply and lack of funding.

competitors.name: Universal Hydrogen
competitors.what: Retrofitted Dash 8 with a hydrogen fuel cell and modular hydrogen capsules
competitors.traction_then: First flight of a Dash 8 with a 1.2 MW fuel cell, March 2023
competitors.funding_then: Not stated in the cited article

competitors.name: ZeroAvia
competitors.what: Hydrogen-electric powertrain of 600 kW for aircraft of up to 19 seats
competitors.traction_then: Flight testing a hydrogen fuel cell aircraft in the first half of 2023
competitors.funding_then: Not stated in the cited article

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires a lightweight high temperature PEM fuel cell propulsion system, hydrogen storage and aircraft certification. A four-person team had to achieve what better funded firms were attempting.

defensibility.rationale: Patent pending propulsion system and airline LOIs, but certification would also be required of every rival and there was no revenue.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy or buy it. The company shut down in August 2026 with no acquirer reported.

market_need_then: Airline decarbonization pressure and regional routes poorly served by battery electric range. YC page cites $145M in LOIs from 7 airlines (letters of intent, not orders).

identity.mascot_or_character: Ground test bed named Clyde and Bonanza demonstrator named Bonnie
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven and ambitious; farewell post titled A Proud Farewell

branding.brand_signature: Playful Bonnie and Clyde names for its two demonstrators
branding.community_and_virality: Aviation trade press (Revolution.aero, Australian Aviation, AIN) covered its milestones, including the first Southern Hemisphere hydrogen-electric taxi in 2026.

brand_strength.rationale: Well covered in aviation trade media but little evidence of a brand driving funding or customers.

pivots.to: Retrofit hydrogen-electric propulsion for existing aircraft and UAVs
pivots.why: Smart Aviation APAC and the company site describe a retrofit program; the YC page describes the original aircraft plan. Reason not found.

outcome_analysis: Stralis built technical demonstrators and won grants and LOIs, but the August 2026 shutdown coverage says it could not raise enough equity and the hydrogen aviation market, certification costs and fuel infrastructure were not ready. A larger seed target of $8M was stated but no close was found. It ended weeks after a successful taxi test, with no acquirer.
notes: The directory status says Active but sources dated August 2026 (ch-aviation, CAPA, AIN) report the company is ceasing operations, so the exit is recorded as shutdown despite the status conflict. Pre-seed of $500K on 2023-04 from Y Combinator and Liquid 2 Ventures is reported only by aggregators (bouncewatch, caplight) and is unverified. Revolution.aero says the pre-seed also had Collab Fund, Schox, Climate Capital and Chris Golda; I did not open that article. Grants listed on the company site have no amounts. Totals conflict ($161K, $1.74M, $2.5M, EUR 591K). Universal Hydrogen and ZeroAvia dates come from search snippets.
